case_title: Imrat Singh & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute (court noted enmity between the two sides; victim had a lot of enemies)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.148; IPC s.302 r/w s.149
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW-10, PW-11); last-seen testimony (PW-6, PW-7); site plan; police investigation record
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.148 and 302 r/w s.149 IPC; life imprisonment for murder, two years RI under s.148, fine Rs.25,000 (default three years RI)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; trial court conviction and sentence upheld
neutral_facts: On 25 May 1994 at about 2 pm, the victim was allegedly beaten with lathis by a group of five accused at a place called Brar Khora, near a path between two villages. Two villagers walking nearby stated that they saw the beating. They said they asked the accused why the victim was being beaten, were threatened, and ran away. They went to their village and later to the police station, where a report was lodged after police visited the spot. Another witness stated that the victim had been called away by one of the accused with an offer of liquor, and a different witness gave a different invitation, offering mutton. A further witness said he was told that one accused and another person had beaten the victim. The victim's body was later found in a jungle or river area, and the witnesses differed on who first reported the death in the village. A site plan was prepared, and the witnesses named as having signed it denied doing so. The victim was reported to have had several enemies, and there was enmity between the two sides. Several persons who were named in the statements, including police personnel and villagers, were not examined as witnesses. The defence disputed the reliability of the eyewitness and last-seen accounts.
physical_harm: Death of the victim (Gajraj Singh) from beating with lathis, as alleged by the prosecution
key_evidence_accepted: None relied on for conviction; Court found eyewitness (PW-10, PW-11) and last-seen (PW-6, PW-7) evidence doubtful due to contradictions
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses PW-10 and PW-11 found unreliable: prepared witnesses, contradictory on attending circumstances, improving statements over time; PW-15 and PW-10 versions totally different
bail_history: Accused on bail at the Supreme Court stage; bail bonds discharged on acquittal
trial_duration: offence: 25.05.1994; trial judgment: 30.03.1995; High Court: 24.10.2008; Supreme Court: 24.10.2019
legal_representation: Accused/appellants: Ms. June Chaudhary, Sr. Adv., with Mohd. Parvez Dabas, Uzmi Jameel Husain, Ms. Shilpa Saini, Shakil Ahmed Syed; Shikhil Suri (Adv., amicus). State: Rahul Kaushik, Ms. Bhuvneshwari Pathak, Ms. Shilpi Satyapriya Satyam
investigation_status: FIR registered after police visited the spot; site plan prepared; investigation found unfair by the Court
procedural_irregularity: Unfair investigation (site plan prepared on instructions from a witness who denied going to the spot and signing; Head Constable and SDOP not examined; important witnesses not examined)
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.148, 302 r/w 149 IPC; High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld; Supreme Court: appeal allowed, acquitted
defence_argument: Eyewitness testimonies of PW-10 and PW-11 untrustworthy and contradictory; PW-6 and PW-7 testimonies contradictory and at best against one accused
legal_principle_applied: Benefit of doubt to accused where material contradictions in witness testimony, non-examination of key witnesses and unfair investigation cast doubt on prosecution case
